facts.fact: USAID's DECA states that in 2015 the Ministry of Communication and Digital Economy (MCEN) was lead architect of Mali Numerique 2020, the country's digital agenda; it names no adopting act or approving body.
The DECA describes Mali Numerique 2020 as the national digital strategy for 2015-2019, a four-year strategy, and says the country has been governed by an outdated one for the past few years.

The DECA says Mali Numerique 2020 set six objectives to be met by 2020, each with action items that were narrowly focused (for example one online portal for digital content, two e-commerce platforms); no cost is given.

The DECA states that more than seven years after the launch of the four-year strategy no final official assessment of its achievements exists, so progress against its objectives cannot be evaluated (as at the document's April 2023 publication date).

The DECA says the government is currently drafting a new digital strategy, referred to as the 2023-2027 digital strategy, and recommends supporting its validation and adoption (as at the document's April 2023 publication date).
